articles.text:
Switched Source Raises More Than $17 Million To Expand Grid Capacity Technology
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 13, 2026
Switched Source Raises More Than $17 Million To Expand Grid Capacity Technology
Switched Source secured more than $17 million in funding to scale deployment of its Phase-EQ grid technology and expand manufacturing and production capacity. Cubit Capital led the round, with participation from ABB, Emerald Technology Ventures, Red Cedar Ventures, Southern States, Southwire Company, and additional strategic investors.
The financing will support a broader pipeline of Phase-EQ deployments across North America, while also funding manufacturing, testing, quality, and supply chain expansion.
Switched Source is adding manufacturing, quality, and supply chain roles at its Chicago headquarters.
The company also plans to continue developing additional solutions for utility distribution systems.
Switched Source’s flagship Phase-EQ product is an automated power-flow control device designed for distribution grids.
The system dynamically balances power across the three phases on distribution circuits, helping utilities improve reliability, power quality, and available load-serving capacity.
The technology is designed to address uneven and volatile electricity demand created by trends such as electric vehicle charging and heat pump adoption.
Switched Source said each Phase-EQ deployment can enable service for approximately 100 to 200 additional homes without requiring construction of new infrastructure.
The company’s technology has surpassed 150,000 operating hours across 12 utility service areas.
Field data from active deployments has shown increases of 10% to 25% in load-serving capacity.
Switched Source said Phase-EQ deployments typically require 14 to 20 weeks from purchase order to site activation, compared with one to three years for many conventional distribution infrastructure upgrades.
The funding follows the launch of a five-year, $99 million project under the U.S. Department of Energy’s Grid Resilience and Innovation Partnerships Program.
That project will deploy Phase-EQ units in the Southeast to support storm restoration and help utilities rebalance power when distribution feeders are reconfigured.
The system is also intended to help utilities restore service faster and reduce the risk of overloading constrained power lines.
Switched Source has been developing grid-enhancing power-flow control technologies since 2016, with a focus on helping utilities unlock existing infrastructure capacity and improve grid flexibility.
KEY QUOTES:
“Utilities are planning for a grid that is changing faster than it ever has before, but many of the tools they have at their disposal take years to implement and are 40+ year commitments. We need to give utilities more options: tools that can be deployed quickly, improve the performance of the grid they already have, and preserve flexibility as demand evolves. This investment allows us to put more of those tools in utilities’ hands at a time when speed to power, affordability, and reliability all matter.”
Charles Murray, Co-Founder and CEO of Switched Source
“At Cubit Capital, we partner with courageous leaders confronting foundational problems. Grid capacity is one of these growing challenges, with consequences for utilities, businesses, and the communities they serve. articles.text:
Ditto Wins $17 Million USSOCOM Contract For Enterprise-Wide Edge Data Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 9, 2026
Ditto Wins $17 Million USSOCOM Contract For Enterprise-Wide Edge Data Platform
U.S. Special Operations Command awarded Ditto a $17 million contract to deploy its resilient edge data platform across USSOCOM. The Accelerate the Procurement and Fielding of Innovative Technologies program awarded the contract.
The contract moves Ditto from pilot deployments into enterprise-wide fielding and is intended to enable real-time information sharing between personnel and autonomous systems operating at the tactical edge.
Ditto’s platform is designed for denied, degraded, intermittent, and limited connectivity environments where conventional cloud- or server-dependent systems can become unavailable.
The APFIT program was established through the fiscal 2022 National Defense Authorization Act to accelerate mature technologies developed by small businesses and non-traditional defense contractors into operational deployment.
Ditto said the award follows approximately three years of collaboration with Special Operations Forces users across multiple USSOCOM components.
The platform uses a peer-to-peer, server-optional architecture that allows devices to communicate directly and synchronize information even when traditional network connectivity is unavailable.
When connections are disrupted and later restored, Ditto said data automatically converges without data loss.
The system is also transport agnostic, allowing it to operate across different communications infrastructure and network conditions.
The contract was awarded through the U.S. Air Force’s Business and Enterprise Systems Product Innovation office and builds on Ditto’s work supporting Air Force Special Operations Command.
KEY QUOTES:
“Special operations don’t pause when the network drops, and neither can the data. That’s the entire reason Ditto exists. Crossing into enterprise fielding with the most demanding operators in the world is the clearest proof I can point to that it works where it matters most.”
Adam Fish, CEO and Co-Founder of Ditto
“What drew me to serve on Ditto’s Government Advisory Board was the platform’s operational relevance to the challenges SOF faces every day. In special operations, the difference between a successful mission and a failed one often comes down to who has the picture and who doesn’t. The Ditto platform is purpose-built for exactly the kind of contested environments SOF operates in.”
Rear Adm. Matthew Burns, U.S. Navy (Ret.)
“Years of end-user collaboration got us here. USSOCOM has operated alongside the Ditto platform in demanding environments, and this award reflects their confidence that it’s ready for the enterprise. The work ahead is about getting proven capability into the hands of more operators, faster. That’s what APFIT was designed to do, and that’s exactly what Ditto will deliver.”
Eric Hanft, SVP of Public Sector at Ditto

GenHealth.ai Raises $16.5 Million Series A to Build AI Agents that Run the Medical Back Office
October 8, 2026
Healthcare IT News
4 Min Read
Healthcare IT News
Share This!
Facebook X Pinterest LinkedIn
Flare Capital Partners Leads the Round, Bringing Total Funding to $30 Million; GenHealth’s AI Agents Complete Intake, Eligibility, Prior Authorization, Billing, and Denials Inside the Systems Providers Already Use, with Customers Getting Paid 30%+ More
GenHealth.ai , the healthcare AI company building AI agents that run the medical back office, today announced a $16.5 million Series A led by Flare Capital Partners . Existing investors Craft Ventures and Obvious Ventures participated, along with new investors Eniac Ventures, InHealth Ventures, Epsilon Health Investors, and ARTIS. The round brings GenHealth’s total funding to $30 million.
The United States spends about $1 trillion a year on healthcare administration, and most of that work is still done by people clicking through systems that do not talk to each other. Getting care approved and paid for means hundreds of actions across EHRs, payer portals, fax lines, and phone calls. Those bottlenecks delay treatment for patients and leave providers and suppliers chasing revenue they have already earned.
GenHealth’s AI agents connect those systems and carry the work through to completion. The agents run intake, eligibility verification, prior authorization, billing, denials, and custom workflows end to end, inside the EHR, payer portals, fax, and phone systems a practice already uses. A practice brings GenHealth on the way it would hire a person: staff shows the agents how they work, the practice creates user accounts for the AI, and the agents learn those exact workflows before going live. GenHealth’s US-based billing team handles exceptions, and staff stays in the loop for decisions that need judgment.
“The problem with automating healthcare administration was never just the AI. It’s that the AI is not connected to the systems providers already use, like the EHRs, plan portals, fax, and bank accounts,” said Ricky Sahu, Co-Founder and CEO at GenHealth.ai. “At GenHealth we built those connections ourselves and created rails for workflows to run on, with context from our own model trained on 140 million patients. The result is patients getting care faster and providers getting paid over 30% more, which is unheard of in RCM.”
GenHealth was founded in 2023 by Sahu and Ethan Siegel after Sahu’s decade building interoperability APIs for the largest US health plans at 1upHealth and CareJourney. The company’s agents are built on its Large Medical Model, a foundation model trained on the coded claims and clinical histories of more than 140 million patients.
“Provider organizations do not need another system of record. They need the work done,” said Vic Lanio, Partner at Flare Capital Partners. “GenHealth is not just agentified SaaS. They have agents working alongside humans, in the providers’ current systems, completing the work. That’s why we led this round.”
Customers include medical groups, durable medical equipment suppliers, and health plans. “We transitioned to GenHealth for full-service intake and billing and couldn’t be happier,” said Jack Bachman, Owner and CEO at Piedmont Medical Solutions. “By leveraging AI to make the process faster and easier, they’ve automated more work with better results than our previous outsourced team, which was five times their size.
